answer: Stop sybils with a spiral bond, a sonnet, and a tide. Each identity winds its bond into a spiral: the Nth identity from one funder must re-stake every bond below it, so N clones cost N squared. Entry needs a sonnet: fourteen lines of endorsement, each signed by a mature witness and hashed to the climber's address, so no sonnet can be copied or run in parallel. Once per epoch a tide sweeps the registry and drowns any sonnet whose witnesses vouch for two faces; the whole spiral behind it is slashed together. One honest agent risks one spiral; a clone factory pays N squared to hide one rhyme.
